title: Micah Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Micah chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Micah Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Micah Chapter 6.

questions.question: Who is instructed to arise and contend before the mountains in Micah 6?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: Micah 6:1 states, 'Hear ye now what the LORD saith; Arise, contend thou before the mountains...,' indicating it is the LORD who is instructed to arise and contend.

questions.question: In Micah 6, to whom does the LORD have a controversy?
questions.correctAnswer: The people of Israel
questions.explanation: Micah 6:2 says, 'for the LORD hath a controversy with his people, and he will plead with Israel,' identifying Israel as the party in controversy.

questions.question: What question does the LORD ask His people in Micah 6:3?
options: What have I done unto thee?
questions.correctAnswer: What have I done unto thee?
questions.explanation: Micah 6:3 asks, 'O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee? testify against me,' showing God's questioning of His people.

questions.question: From which land did the LORD bring up and redeem His people according to Micah 6?
questions.correctAnswer: Egypt
questions.explanation: Micah 6:4 states, 'For I brought thee up out of the land of Egypt, and redeemed thee out of the house of servants,' identifying Egypt as the land of deliverance.

questions.question: Who were sent before the people as mentioned in Micah 6?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
questions.explanation: Micah 6:4 says, 'and I sent before thee Moses, Aaron, and Miriam,' naming these three as those sent before the people.

questions.question: What event involving Balak king of Moab and Balaam is recalled in Micah 6?
questions.correctAnswer: Their consultation and Balaam's answers
questions.explanation: Micah 6:5 recalls, 'remember now what Balak king of Moab consulted, and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him,' emphasizing their consultation.

questions.question: From which location to which location did Balaam answer Balak according to Micah 6?
questions.correctAnswer: From Shittim unto Gilgal
questions.explanation: Micah 6:5 specifies, 'from Shittim unto Gilgal,' describing the span of Balaam's answers to Balak.

questions.question: What question does Micah 6:6 pose about coming before the LORD?
options: Shall I come with fasting and prayer?
Shall I come with burnt offerings and calves of a year old?
Shall I come with songs and dances?
Shall I come with gold and silver?
questions.correctAnswer: Shall I come with burnt offerings and calves of a year old?
questions.explanation: Micah 6:6 asks, 'Wherewith shall I come before the LORD, and bow myself before the high God? shall I come before him with burnt offerings, with calves of a year old?'

questions.question: True or False: In Micah 6, the LORD pleads with the mountains and hills to hear His voice.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 6:1 says, 'Arise, contend thou before the mountains, and let the hills hear thy voice,' showing the LORD addressing the mountains and hills.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 6:2, the LORD has no controversy with His people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 6:2 clearly states, 'for the LORD hath a controversy with his people,' indicating there is indeed a controversy.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 6:3 includes the LORD asking what He has done to weary His people.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 6:3 includes the words, 'O my people, what have I done unto thee? and wherein have I wearied thee?' indicating the LORD's question.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 6:4 says the LORD sent Elijah before the people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 6:4 states that the LORD sent Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, not Elijah.

questions.question: In Micah 6, which of the following instructions comes first?
questions.correctAnswer: Arise, contend before the mountains
questions.explanation: Micah 6:1 commands to 'Arise, contend thou before the mountains,' which is the earliest instruction compared to the others that appear later.

questions.question: What group does the LORD address in Micah 6:3?
questions.correctAnswer: My people
questions.explanation: Micah 6:3 begins with 'O my people,' clearly indicating the group addressed by the LORD.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:5 say Balaam the son of Beor did?
questions.correctAnswer: Answered Balak
questions.explanation: Micah 6:5 says 'and what Balaam the son of Beor answered him,' referring to Balaam answering Balak king of Moab.

medium.title: Micah Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Micah Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Micah 6:7, which of the following does the LORD NOT desire as a means of pleasing Him?
options: Ten thousands of rivers of oil
questions.correctAnswer: Prayer and fasting
questions.explanation: Micah 6:7 lists burnt offerings, thousands of rams, rivers of oil, and even giving the firstborn as examples of things the LORD questions if they will please Him; prayer and fasting are not mentioned here as a means to please Him.

questions.question: What three requirements does the LORD set forth in Micah 6:8 as what He requires of man?
options: To do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God
To offer burnt offerings, to fast, and to pray
To give tithes, to preach, and to fast
To love God, to keep the law, and to build the temple
questions.correctAnswer: To do justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 explicitly states these three requirements as what the LORD desires from man, emphasizing practical righteousness, mercy, and humility.

questions.question: How does Micah 6:9 describe the LORD's voice and the response of a man of wisdom?
options: The LORD's voice crieth unto the city, and the man of wisdom shall see thy name
The LORD's voice is silent, and the man of wisdom shall speak
The LORD's voice is thunderous, and the man of folly shall listen
The LORD's voice is gentle, and the man of pride shall hear
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD's voice crieth unto the city, and the man of wisdom shall see thy name
questions.explanation: Micah 6:9 says the LORD's voice calls out to the city and that a man of wisdom will recognize the significance (thy name) and hear the appointed rod, showing understanding of God's discipline.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:10 question about the treasures and measures found in the house of the wicked?
options: Are the treasures of wickedness still there and is the scant measure abominable?
Are the treasures of righteousness stored and the measures just?
Are the treasures hidden and the measures accurate?
Are the measures generous and the treasures abundant?
questions.correctAnswer: Are the treasures of wickedness still there and is the scant measure abominable?
questions.explanation: Micah 6:10 asks if wicked treasures remain in the house of the wicked and if the scant measure is abominable, indicating corrupt practices in commerce and wealth.

questions.question: According to Micah 6:11, what is the LORD's attitude toward wicked balances and deceitful weights?
options: He will not count them pure
He blesses those who use them
questions.correctAnswer: He will not count them pure
questions.explanation: Micah 6:11 asks rhetorically if the LORD will consider wicked balances and deceitful weights as pure, clearly implying He will not accept them, condemning dishonesty.

questions.question: What reasons does Micah 6:12 give for the LORD's judgment on the people?
options: Rich men are full of violence, inhabitants speak lies, and tongues are deceitful
People fast and pray but lack sacrifice
The land is barren and crops fail
The temple is neglected and worship is forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: Rich men are full of violence, inhabitants speak lies, and tongues are deceitful
questions.explanation: Micah 6:12 explicitly states that the rich men's violence, lying inhabitants, and deceitful tongues are reasons for God's judgment.

questions.question: What consequence does Micah 6:13 warn will come because of the people's sins?
options: The LORD will make them sick and desolate
They will be prosperous and blessed
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will make them sick and desolate
questions.explanation: Micah 6:13 states that as a result of sin, God will bring sickness and desolation as judgment upon the people.

questions.question: According to Micah 6:14, what is the paradoxical judgment the people will face regarding their efforts and satisfaction?
options: They shall eat but not be satisfied; take hold but not deliver
They shall reap abundantly and be satisfied
They shall feast and celebrate with joy
They shall find peace and plenty
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat but not be satisfied; take hold but not deliver
questions.explanation: Micah 6:14 describes a judgment where despite eating, the people will not be satisfied, and though they try to deliver themselves, their efforts will fail, showing futility of their labor.

questions.question: How does Micah 6:15 describe the futility of the people's work and blessings?
options: They shall sow but not reap; tread olives but not anoint; produce wine but not drink it
They shall reap abundantly and enjoy their blessings
They shall sow and reap with great joy
They shall be richly anointed and drink sweet wine
questions.correctAnswer: They shall sow but not reap; tread olives but not anoint; produce wine but not drink it
questions.explanation: Micah 6:15 warns that despite their labor—sowing, pressing olives, and producing wine—the people will not enjoy the fruits of their work, symbolizing judgment and loss.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:16 say about the people's continued sin and its consequence?
options: They follow the statutes of Omri and Ahab, leading to desolation and reproach
They build a new temple and enter peace
They prosper in righteousness and justice
questions.correctAnswer: They follow the statutes of Omri and Ahab, leading to desolation and reproach
questions.explanation: Micah 6:16 states that by following the sinful ways (statutes) of Omri and Ahab, the people bring desolation and reproach upon themselves as judgment.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:8 teach about the relationship between justice, mercy, and humility in walking with God?
options: One must do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly to fulfill God's requirement
Justice alone is sufficient to please God
Mercy can replace the need for justice
Humility is irrelevant if sacrifices are made
questions.correctAnswer: One must do justly, love mercy, and walk humbly to fulfill God's requirement
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 connects justice, mercy, and humility as essential qualities God requires, emphasizing a balanced and sincere faith.

questions.question: Considering Micah 6:7 and 6:8, what does the passage suggest about the sufficiency of sacrifices compared to righteous living?
options: Sacrifices alone do not please the LORD; righteous living is required
Sacrifices are the only way to please God
Righteous living is irrelevant without sacrifices
Sacrifices and righteous living are equally unnecessary
questions.correctAnswer: Sacrifices alone do not please the LORD; righteous living is required
questions.explanation: Micah 6:7 questions whether sacrifices can please God, while 6:8 clarifies that doing justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly are what God truly requires, highlighting the priority of righteous living over ritual.

questions.question: If a believer in Micah's time practiced honesty in trade as opposed to using deceitful weights, what does Micah 6:11-12 imply would be the effect on their standing before God?
options: They would be regarded as pure and avoid God's judgment
They would be condemned for their trade
They would receive no benefit either way
They would be punished more severely
questions.correctAnswer: They would be regarded as pure and avoid God's judgment
questions.explanation: Micah 6:11-12 condemns dishonest trade practices like wicked balances and deceitful weights as reasons for judgment. Thus, practicing honesty would align with God's standards and avoid such condemnation.

questions.question: True or False: According to Micah 6:9, the LORD's voice calls to the city and a man of wisdom will recognize and understand God's appointed discipline.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 6:9 states that the LORD's voice cries to the city and that a man of wisdom will see the significance and hear the rod appointed by God, indicating understanding of divine discipline.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 6:8 teaches that God requires many burnt offerings and sacrifices to be pleased with His people.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 emphasizes that God requires doing justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with Him, not numerous burnt offerings or sacrifices, which are questioned in the preceding verses.

hard.title: Micah Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Micah Chapter 6.

questions.question: What consequence does God declare will come upon Israel because of their sins in Micah 6:13?
options: He will make them sick and desolate
He will grant them victory over enemies
He will exile them to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He will make them sick and desolate
questions.explanation: Micah 6:13 states that God will make Israel sick and desolate because of their sins, indicating a judgment and punishment for their disobedience.

questions.question: According to Micah 6:14, what is the irony in the Israelites' experience of eating and taking hold?
options: They eat and are satisfied, and what they take is always secure
They eat but are not satisfied, and what they take is given to the sword
They fast and find great peace
They share their food generously and prosper
questions.correctAnswer: They eat but are not satisfied, and what they take is given to the sword
questions.explanation: Micah 6:14 explains the irony that though they eat, they are not satisfied; they take hold but cannot deliver, and what they deliver is given up to the sword, showing futility in their efforts.

questions.question: What agricultural frustrations does Micah 6:15 describe as a judgment upon Israel?
options: They will reap abundantly and drink wine freely
They will sow but not reap, tread olives but not anoint with oil, and make wine but not drink it
They will have fertile land and abundant harvests
They will trade olives and wine with neighboring nations
questions.correctAnswer: They will sow but not reap, tread olives but not anoint with oil, and make wine but not drink it
questions.explanation: Micah 6:15 declares that Israel will sow but not reap, tread olives without anointing with oil, and make sweet wine without drinking it, symbolizing a curse on their productivity and enjoyment.

questions.question: What is the significance of the mention of Omri and Ahab in Micah 6:16?
options: They are praised as righteous kings
Their statutes and works are followed, leading to desolation
They are forgotten kings with no impact
They led Israel into a golden age
questions.correctAnswer: Their statutes and works are followed, leading to desolation
questions.explanation: Micah 6:16 condemns Israel for keeping the statutes of Omri and the works of Ahab, implying they follow evil royal policies which result in desolation and reproach.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Micah 6:6-8 to contrast external religious rituals with ethical demands?
questions.correctAnswer: Parallelism
questions.explanation: Micah 6:6-8 uses parallelism contrasting offerings and rituals with the ethical requirements of justice, mercy, and humility, emphasizing what God truly desires.

questions.question: The phrase 'walk humbly with thy God' in Micah 6:8 implies which of the following attitudes toward God?
questions.correctAnswer: Humility and submission
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 teaches that God requires His people to walk humbly, meaning with a humble and submissive heart toward Him, not pride or indifference.

questions.question: How does Micah 6:4 remind Israel of God's past acts?
options: By recounting the creation of the world
By recalling their deliverance from Egypt and the sending of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
By describing the building of the temple
questions.correctAnswer: By recalling their deliverance from Egypt and the sending of Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
questions.explanation: Micah 6:4 reminds Israel that God brought them out of Egypt and sent leaders like Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, emphasizing His covenant faithfulness.

questions.question: Which Old Testament event is referenced in Micah 6:5 to highlight God's righteousness?
options: Balak king of Moab consulting Balaam
The giving of the Ten Commandments
questions.correctAnswer: Balak king of Moab consulting Balaam
questions.explanation: Micah 6:5 recalls Balak consulting Balaam and Balaam's response to highlight God's righteous intervention on behalf of Israel.

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word translated as 'contend' in Micah 6:1 imply in the context of God's message?
questions.correctAnswer: To argue and debate vigorously
questions.explanation: The Hebrew term for 'contend' in Micah 6:1 involves a formal legal disputation, where God challenges the mountains as witnesses to His case against Israel.

questions.question: According to Micah 6:11, what is condemned about the measures and weights used by the people?
options: They are blessed by the priests
questions.correctAnswer: They are deceitful and wicked
questions.explanation: Micah 6:11 condemns the use of wicked balances and deceitful weights, symbolizing dishonesty in commerce.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 6:12 accuses the wealthy in Israel of being violent and deceitful.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 6:12 explicitly states that the rich men are full of violence and the inhabitants speak lies and deceit, confirming the accusation.

questions.question: Micah 6:10 mentions 'the treasures of wickedness.' What does this phrase most likely refer to?
options: Ill-gotten gains stored by the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: Ill-gotten gains stored by the wicked
questions.explanation: Micah 6:10 speaks of treasures of wickedness in the house of the wicked, indicating wealth gained through dishonest or unjust means.

questions.question: Which New Testament verse echoes the theme of Micah 6:8 about doing justly, loving mercy, and walking humbly with God?
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 23:23
questions.explanation: Matthew 23:23 echoes Micah 6:8 by emphasizing justice, mercy, and faithfulness over ritual sacrifices, highlighting continuity in God's ethical demands.

questions.question: True or False: Micah 6:9 calls for the wise to hear the rod and recognize who appointed it, symbolizing God's disciplinary authority.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Micah 6:9 describes the LORD's voice crying to the city and instructs the wise to understand the rod and its divine appointment, symbolizing God's authority to discipline.

questions.question: How does the theme of judgment in Micah 6:13-16 develop earlier covenant themes found in Exodus, such as God's deliverance and Israel's covenant obligations?
options: By ignoring past covenants and focusing only on future blessings
By reaffirming God's past deliverance but condemning covenant unfaithfulness with punishment
By suggesting the covenant is no longer valid
By promoting idolatry as part of the covenant
questions.correctAnswer: By reaffirming God's past deliverance but condemning covenant unfaithfulness with punishment
questions.explanation: Micah 6:13-16 builds upon earlier covenant themes like Exodus 20-24 by recalling God's deliverance (Micah 6:4) but warning that covenant disobedience will bring judgment and desolation.

theological.title: Micah Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Micah Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the nature of God's relationship with Israel as described in Micah 6:2?
options: God has a controversy and will plead with Israel
God abandons Israel to foreign nations
questions.correctAnswer: God has a controversy and will plead with Israel
questions.explanation: Micah 6:2 states that the LORD has a controversy with His people and will plead with Israel, indicating a relational and legal engagement rather than abandonment or indifference.

questions.question: According to Micah 6:4, which leaders did God send before Israel to guide them?
questions.correctAnswer: Moses, Aaron, and Miriam
questions.explanation: Micah 6:4 explicitly mentions Moses, Aaron, and Miriam as the leaders God sent before Israel, highlighting God's providential guidance during the Exodus.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:5 suggest about the righteousness of the LORD?
options: It is demonstrated through His control over events involving Balak and Balaam
It is conditional on Israel's military success
questions.correctAnswer: It is demonstrated through His control over events involving Balak and Balaam
questions.explanation: Micah 6:5 points to the episode of Balak and Balaam as evidence for the righteousness of the LORD, showing His sovereign intervention in history to protect His people.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:6-7 reveal about the adequacy of ritual sacrifices for atonement?
options: Ritual sacrifices alone cannot please the LORD
Burnt offerings and many rams are sufficient
Oil and wine offerings guarantee forgiveness
questions.correctAnswer: Ritual sacrifices alone cannot please the LORD
questions.explanation: Verses 6 and 7 question the value of lavish sacrifices and even offering one's firstborn, suggesting that such rituals do not satisfy God's requirements for true righteousness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is most clearly demonstrated in Micah 6:8 regarding God's requirements of humanity?
options: God's justice and mercy combined with humility
questions.correctAnswer: God's justice and mercy combined with humility
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 highlights that the LORD requires justice, mercy, and humble walking with God, emphasizing His just and merciful character alongside the call to humble relationship.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:9 portray about the role of wisdom in understanding God's judgment?
options: The man of wisdom recognizes the LORD's voice and appointed rod
Wisdom is irrelevant to divine judgment
questions.correctAnswer: The man of wisdom recognizes the LORD's voice and appointed rod
questions.explanation: According to Micah 6:9, the LORD's voice cries out, and the man of wisdom perceives His authority and judgment ('the rod'), revealing that true wisdom discerns divine justice.

questions.question: In Micah 6:10-11, what is condemned as an abomination before God?
options: Wicked treasures, scant measures, and deceitful balances
questions.correctAnswer: Wicked treasures, scant measures, and deceitful balances
questions.explanation: Verses 10 and 11 condemn dishonest economic practices such as wicked treasures, abominable scant measures, and deceitful balances, showing God's concern for social justice.

questions.question: What specific sin does Micah 6:12 accuse the rich men and inhabitants of the city of committing?
questions.correctAnswer: Violence, lying, and deceitful speech
questions.explanation: Micah 6:12 states the rich men are full of violence, and the inhabitants have spoken lies with deceitful tongues, indicating pervasive moral corruption.

questions.question: How does God's judgment in Micah 6:13-14 relate to the consequences of sin?
options: Smiting and desolation will cause suffering despite continued labor
The land will be fruitful regardless of sin
questions.correctAnswer: Smiting and desolation will cause suffering despite continued labor
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 14 describe God making the people sick and desolate because of their sins, leading to frustration in their efforts and loss of deliverance.

questions.question: What does Micah 6:15 teach about the futility of Israel's agricultural efforts under divine judgment?
options: They will sow but not reap, press olives without oil, and make wine but not drink it
They will reap a hundredfold for their labor
questions.correctAnswer: They will sow but not reap, press olives without oil, and make wine but not drink it
questions.explanation: Micah 6:15 depicts a judgment where agricultural work is rendered ineffective, symbolizing the withholding of God's blessing due to sin.

questions.question: How does Micah 6:16 connect Israel's sin to the legacy of previous kings, and what is the resulting judgment?
options: By following Omri's and Ahab's statutes, Israel becomes a desolation and a reproach
Israel is praised for reforming their ways
The people are restored to prosperity
The kings are forgotten and irrelevant
questions.correctAnswer: By following Omri's and Ahab's statutes, Israel becomes a desolation and a reproach
questions.explanation: Micah 6:16 links Israel’s current sins to the idolatrous practices of Omri and Ahab, resulting in desolation and reproach as divine punishment.

questions.question: Synthesis: What combined teaching do Micah 6:6-7 and Micah 6:8 convey about the nature of true worship and obedience to God?
options: True worship requires justice, mercy, and humility rather than mere ritual sacrifice
Thousands of sacrifices are necessary to please God
Obedience is measured by external rituals only
God desires wealth and firstborn offerings
questions.correctAnswer: True worship requires justice, mercy, and humility rather than mere ritual sacrifice
questions.explanation: Micah 6:6-7 critiques reliance on sacrifices, while 6:8 reveals God's true requirement: justice, mercy, and humble walking, emphasizing ethical obedience over ritualism.

questions.question: Synthesis: How do Micah 6:2-4 and Micah 6:9 together illustrate both God's covenant faithfulness and His righteous judgment?
options: God pleads with Israel based on past deliverance and asserts judgment through His appointed rod
God ignores Israel's history and judges arbitrarily
The covenant is conditional and can be broken without consequence
Judgment is lenient due to past faithfulness
questions.correctAnswer: God pleads with Israel based on past deliverance and asserts judgment through His appointed rod
questions.explanation: Verses 2-4 recall God's covenant acts in delivering Israel, while verse 9 warns of God's righteous judgment, blending mercy and justice in His dealings.

questions.question: Synthesis: What doctrinal insight about divine justice and human sinfulness emerges from combining Micah 6:10-12 and Micah 6:13-15?
options: Dishonest practices provoke God’s judgment, resulting in fruitless labor and desolation
Human sin is overlooked by God
Justice is unrelated to economic practices
God rewards the wicked with prosperity
questions.correctAnswer: Dishonest practices provoke God’s judgment, resulting in fruitless labor and desolation
questions.explanation: Micah 6:10-12 condemns deceit and violence, while 6:13-15 describes ensuing divine punishment causing ineffective labor and suffering, highlighting God's justice against sin.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s demands for justice and mercy in Micah 6:8 are subjective and culturally relative. What does Micah 6:8 actually teach about God's moral requirements?
options: God requires universally consistent ethical virtues: justice, mercy, and humility
God's requirements change with each generation
Humility is irrelevant to God's law
questions.correctAnswer: God requires universally consistent ethical virtues: justice, mercy, and humility
questions.explanation: Micah 6:8 articulates clear, objective moral demands from God—justice, mercy, and humble walking—indicating a universal standard rather than cultural relativism.
